segments.zh: Overnight, hackers pushed supermarket fridges
to fifty degrees Celsius.
segments.en: 把超市冰箱烧到了五十度。

segments.zh: Fifty degrees.
Hotter than a car in the summer sun.
According to AP, about seven hundred French supermarkets were hit in October,
segments.en: 据美联社，十月份法国约七百家超市中招，

segments.zh: out of roughly ten thousand.
Late October, a new wave hit Europe.
Reportedly chains in Belgium and Ireland too.
segments.en: 据报道比利时、爱尔兰的连锁店也遭殃。

segments.zh: Today's brain teaser:
a fridge makes cold, so how can it turn into an oven?
segments.en: 冰箱是制冷的，凭啥能变成烤箱？

segments.zh: Meet our hero, Frosty,
a supermarket fridge.
Twist one: a fridge does not make cold at all.
segments.en: 反转一：冰箱根本不“造冷”。

segments.zh: There is no such stuff as cold.
There is only more heat or less heat.
Cold is just molecules jiggling slowly.
Heat is the same molecules jiggling fast.
segments.en: 热，是同样的分子晃得快。

segments.zh: A fridge's job
is to throw heat from inside to outside.
segments.en: 是把热从里面赶到外面。

segments.zh: It is like a bouncer,
showing heat out the back door, one by one.
Don't believe it? Touch the back of your fridge.
It's warm.
In fact, a fridge heats your kitchen.
segments.en: 其实冰箱一直在给厨房加热，

segments.zh: It dumps the food's heat, plus its own motor's heat.
segments.en: 吐出的是食物的热，加上电机自己的热。

segments.zh: How?
With a fluid that keeps moving, called refrigerant.
segments.en: 靠一种会“跑”的液体，叫制冷剂。

segments.zh: Inside, it boils off
and soaks up heat.
Like sweat:
when it evaporates, you cool down.
Then the compressor squeezes it,
and the coils out back dump the heat.
segments.en: 在背后的管子里把热吐出去。

segments.zh: Round and round.
The bouncer never clocks out.
So, open the fridge to cool your kitchen?
segments.en: 所以开着冰箱门给厨房降温？

segments.zh: The room only gets warmer.
Twist two: the bouncer takes orders from a computer.
segments.en: 反转二：保安是听电脑指挥的。

segments.zh: Supermarket fridges are linked to a control system.
segments.en: 超市的冰柜连着一套控制系统，

segments.zh: You can set the temperature remotely.
According to AP, the software was from Danfoss, a Danish company.
segments.en: 据美联社，系统来自丹麦的丹佛斯公司，

segments.zh: Most hit systems were old, no longer updated.
segments.en: 中招的多是老设备，早就不再更新。

segments.zh: The lock was broken and never fixed,
so hackers slipped in over the internet.
segments.en: 黑客就从网上溜了进来。

segments.zh: Like leaving your key under the doormat,
segments.en: 像把家门钥匙压在门垫下，

segments.zh: then posting your address online.
Why put a fridge online at all?
So one person can watch hundreds of stores from one screen.
segments.en: 好让一个人在一块屏幕上，盯住几百家店。

segments.zh: So how did they reach fifty degrees?
This part is our guess.
Fridges actually contain heaters,
segments.en: 冰柜里本来就有加热丝，

segments.zh: for melting frost.
Turn the bouncer off and leave the heaters on,
segments.en: 要是保安被关掉、加热丝一直开着，

segments.zh: and the fridge becomes a small oven.
segments.en: 冰柜就成了一个小烤箱。

segments.zh: Reportedly some stores even had fires.
segments.en: 据报道，有的店还冒了火，

segments.zh: The cause is still being investigated.
Twist three, the scariest part is not the heat.
segments.en: 反转三，最吓人的不是热，

segments.zh: It is the bacteria.
The USDA calls four to sixty degrees Celsius the danger zone.
segments.en: 美国农业部说，四度到六十度是“危险区”。

segments.zh: In that zone, bacteria can double
in about twenty minutes.
One becomes two, two become four.
segments.en: 一个变两个，两个变四个，

segments.zh: Overnight, that is an astronomical number.
A doubling every twenty minutes
is seventy-two doublings a day, on paper.
segments.en: 一天就是七十二次翻倍，这是纸上算的。

segments.zh: So meat and milk that sat warm overnight
segments.en: 所以热过一夜的肉和奶，

segments.zh: have to be thrown out.
Cold doesn't kill bacteria.
It just puts them to sleep.
That's why frozen meat, once thawed,
lets the bacteria wake up and grow again.
When the bouncer clocks out,
the bacteria throw a party.
Fine print: seven hundred stores and fifty degrees come from news reports.
segments.en: 友情提示：七百家、五十度来自新闻报道；

segments.zh: How the heaters were switched on is our guess.
segments.en: 加热丝怎么被打开，是我们的推测。

segments.zh: France's finance minister said food supply was never at risk.
segments.en: 法国财长说，食品供应没有风险。

segments.zh: According to AP, the advice from Danfoss is boring:
segments.en: 据美联社，丹佛斯的建议很朴素：

segments.zh: keep it updated, and put it behind a firewall.
segments.en: 及时更新，再加一道防火墙。

segments.zh: So how does a fridge become an oven?
It never made cold. It only moves heat.
segments.en: 因为它从来不造冷，只会搬热。

segments.zh: The cold was never in the fridge.
It was just heat, shown the door.
